title: Random or multiple cylinder misfire detected
meaning: The engine is misfiring in one or more cylinders. Fuel may not be burning evenly, which can make the engine shake or lose power.
safeToDriveNote: If the check-engine light is flashing or the engine is shaking, stop driving when safe; continued driving can damage the catalytic converter. Otherwise, arrange prompt diagnosis.

causes.name: Worn or fouled spark plugs
causes.notes: A common first check, especially if service is overdue.

causes.name: Ignition coil or coil wiring fault
causes.notes: May affect one or several cylinders.

causes.name: Fuel delivery problem
causes.notes: Pressure or injector issues can cause uneven combustion.

causes.name: Vacuum leak or low compression
causes.notes: Consider after basic ignition and fuel checks.

mechanicChecklist: Check for a flashing warning light and note when the misfire occurs
Review freeze-frame data and misfire counts by cylinder
Inspect plugs, coils, wiring, and fuel trims before replacing parts
dontReplaceYet: Catalytic converter before the misfire is fixed
All ignition coils without cylinder-specific test results

title: Cylinder 1 misfire detected
meaning: Cylinder 1 is not burning its fuel and air mixture consistently. You may notice a rough idle, vibration, or reduced power.
safeToDriveNote: Flashing check-engine light or heavy shaking: stop driving as soon as it's safe. Unburned fuel can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter. Steady light with a mild rough idle: short, gentle drives to get it checked are generally okay. Avoid hard acceleration, towing, and long trips. Don't clear the code and keep driving.

causes.name: Worn or fouled spark plug
causes.notes: Most common cause and cheapest to rule out.

causes.name: Ignition coil or boot
causes.notes: A swap test can help confirm whether the fault follows the coil.

causes.name: Injector fault or carbon deposits, especially on direct-injection engines
causes.notes: Contaminated fuel usually causes misfires on several cylinders at once.

causes.name: Intake or vacuum leak near that cylinder
causes.notes: Check after basic ignition and fuel tests; relative cost can range from low to medium.

causes.name: Low compression from valves, rings, or head gasket
causes.notes: Test compression before considering engine parts.

mechanicChecklist: Check cylinder 1 misfire counts and freeze-frame data
Inspect or test the cylinder 1 plug, coil, and connections
If needed, test injector operation and compression
dontReplaceYet: All coils or injectors before a swap test
The catalytic converter before the misfire is fixed
Engine parts before compression is tested
Clearing the code and ignoring it is not a fix

quickCheck.title: Coil swap test
steps: Swap the cylinder 1 coil with the cylinder 2 coil.
Clear the code, drive normally, and re-read codes.
If the code changes to P0302, the coil is the problem.
If it stays P0301, check the spark plug and injector next.
quickCheck.caution: Coil access varies by engine, and cylinder 1's location varies, so check the service manual.

driverQuestions: Does it happen on cold start, under load, or both?
Any recent plug, coil, or fuel changes?

title: Cylinder 2 misfire detected
meaning: Cylinder 2 is not burning its fuel and air mixture consistently. You may notice a rough idle, vibration, or reduced power.
safeToDriveNote: If the check-engine light is flashing or the engine runs roughly, stop driving when safe and get prompt help; a misfire can damage emissions components.

causes.name: Spark plug worn or fouled on cylinder 2
Ignition coil or boot fault on cylinder 2
causes.notes: A swap test can help confirm whether the fault follows the coil.

causes.name: Low compression or air leak
causes.notes: Check if ignition and fuel tests do not explain the fault.

mechanicChecklist: Check cylinder 2 misfire counts and freeze-frame data
Inspect or test the cylinder 2 plug, coil, and connections
If needed, test injector operation and compression
dontReplaceYet: Catalytic converter before correcting the misfire
Engine parts before confirming compression is low

title: Cylinder 3 misfire detected
meaning: Cylinder 3 is not burning its fuel and air mixture consistently. You may notice a rough idle, vibration, or reduced power.
safeToDriveNote: If the check-engine light is flashing or the engine runs roughly, stop driving when safe and get prompt help; a misfire can damage emissions components.

causes.name: Spark plug worn or fouled on cylinder 3
Ignition coil or boot fault on cylinder 3
causes.notes: A swap test can help confirm whether the fault follows the coil.

causes.name: Low compression or air leak
causes.notes: Check if ignition and fuel tests do not explain the fault.

mechanicChecklist: Check cylinder 3 misfire counts and freeze-frame data
Inspect or test the cylinder 3 plug, coil, and connections
If needed, test injector operation and compression
dontReplaceYet: Catalytic converter before correcting the misfire
Engine parts before confirming compression is low

title: Cylinder 4 misfire detected
meaning: Cylinder 4 is not burning its fuel and air mixture consistently. You may notice a rough idle, vibration, or reduced power.
safeToDriveNote: If the check-engine light is flashing or the engine runs roughly, stop driving when safe and get prompt help; a misfire can damage emissions components.

causes.name: Spark plug worn or fouled on cylinder 4
Ignition coil or boot fault on cylinder 4
causes.notes: A swap test can help confirm whether the fault follows the coil.

causes.name: Low compression or air leak
causes.notes: Check if ignition and fuel tests do not explain the fault.

mechanicChecklist: Check cylinder 4 misfire counts and freeze-frame data
Inspect or test the cylinder 4 plug, coil, and connections
If needed, test injector operation and compression
dontReplaceYet: Catalytic converter before correcting the misfire
Engine parts before confirming compression is low

title: System too lean (Bank 1)
meaning: The engine computer is detecting too much air, or too little fuel, on bank 1. This can affect idle, power, or fuel economy.
safeToDriveNote: It is typically possible to drive a short distance if the engine runs normally, but have it checked soon; stop if it stalls, overheats, or runs very roughly.

causes.name: Unmetered air from a vacuum or intake leak
Dirty or under-reading mass airflow sensor
causes.notes: Verify readings and wiring before replacement.

causes.name: Low fuel pressure or restricted delivery
Exhaust leak ahead of an oxygen sensor

mechanicChecklist: Review fuel trims at idle and raised rpm
Smoke-test the intake for leaks
Verify MAF readings and fuel pressure
dontReplaceYet: Oxygen sensors before checking for air leaks and fuel pressure
MAF sensor without testing its readings and wiring

title: System too rich (Bank 1)
meaning: The engine computer is detecting too much fuel, or too little air, on bank 1. This may increase fuel use or cause rough running.
safeToDriveNote: A short trip is typically reasonable if it runs normally, but arrange a check soon; stop if it smells strongly of fuel, stalls, or runs roughly.

causes.name: Fuel injector leaking or delivering too much fuel
causes.notes: Check fuel pressure and injector balance.

causes.name: Purge valve stuck open
causes.notes: Can change mixture, especially after refueling.

mechanicChecklist: Review fuel trims and freeze-frame data
Check fuel pressure and injector leakage
Verify MAF readings and purge valve operation
dontReplaceYet: Oxygen sensors without checking mixture and fuel pressure
Fuel injectors as a set without test results

title: Catalyst system efficiency below threshold (Bank 1)
meaning: The exhaust readings suggest the catalytic converter may not be cleaning exhaust as expected. The code alone does not prove the converter has failed.
safeToDriveNote: It is typically possible to drive if the vehicle runs normally, but have it checked; stop if the warning flashes, power drops, or the vehicle overheats.

causes.name: Exhaust leak near the converter or sensors
causes.notes: Check leaks before judging sensor or converter performance.

causes.name: Faulty oxygen sensor or wiring
causes.notes: Compare sensor signals and inspect wiring.

causes.name: Unresolved misfire or rich/lean condition
causes.notes: Can damage or confuse catalyst monitoring.

mechanicChecklist: Check for exhaust leaks and other engine codes
Review upstream and downstream oxygen sensor data
Confirm converter efficiency after fixing mixture or misfire issues
dontReplaceYet: Catalytic converter before ruling out leaks, sensor faults, and engine-running issues
Oxygen sensors without checking live data

title: Catalyst system efficiency below threshold (Bank 2)
meaning: The exhaust readings suggest the catalytic converter on bank 2 may not be cleaning exhaust as expected. The code alone does not prove the converter has failed.
safeToDriveNote: It is typically possible to drive if the vehicle runs normally, but have it checked; stop if the warning flashes, power drops, or the vehicle overheats.

causes.name: Exhaust leak near the converter or sensors
causes.notes: Check leaks before judging sensor or converter performance.

causes.name: Faulty oxygen sensor or wiring
causes.notes: Compare sensor signals and inspect wiring.

causes.name: Unresolved misfire or rich/lean condition
causes.notes: Can damage or confuse catalyst monitoring.

mechanicChecklist: Check for exhaust leaks and other engine codes
Review bank 2 oxygen sensor data
Confirm converter efficiency after fixing mixture or misfire issues
dontReplaceYet: Catalytic converter before ruling out leaks, sensor faults, and engine-running issues
Oxygen sensors without checking live data

title: Evaporative emission system leak detected (small leak)
meaning: The system that keeps fuel vapors contained has detected a small leak. A loose fuel cap is one simple possibility, but not the only one.
safeToDriveNote: The vehicle is typically drivable if it runs normally; check the fuel cap and schedule diagnosis if the light stays on. Fuel vapor odor needs prompt attention.

causes.name: Fuel cap loose, damaged, or seal worn
causes.notes: Refit until secure; inspect its seal.

causes.name: Small leak in vapor hose or connection
causes.notes: A smoke test can locate small leaks.

causes.name: EVAP valve or canister seal issue

mechanicChecklist: Refit and inspect the fuel cap
Check EVAP hoses and connections
Smoke-test the system if the code returns
dontReplaceYet: EVAP canister before locating the leak
Purge or vent valves without test results

title: Evaporative emission system large leak detected
meaning: The fuel-vapor containment system detected a large leak or could not seal during its test. A loose or missing fuel cap is a common first check.
safeToDriveNote: It is typically drivable if there is no fuel smell and the engine runs normally; refit the cap and have it checked if the light returns. Avoid driving with a strong fuel odor.

causes.name: Fuel cap loose, missing, or damaged
Purge or vent valve not sealing

mechanicChecklist: Check fuel cap and filler neck
Inspect EVAP hoses and electrical connections
Run a smoke test and valve test
dontReplaceYet: EVAP canister before finding the leak
Fuel tank before checking cap, hoses, and valves

title: Evaporative emission system very small leak detected
meaning: The vapor-control system detected a very small leak. The cap seal and tiny hose or valve leaks are common places to begin checking.
safeToDriveNote: It is typically drivable if there is no fuel odor and the vehicle runs normally; check the cap and arrange diagnosis if the warning persists.

causes.name: Fuel cap seal or filler-neck sealing surface
Small EVAP hose or seal leak
causes.notes: A smoke test may be needed.

causes.name: Purge or vent valve not sealing fully

mechanicChecklist: Inspect and refit the fuel cap
Inspect filler neck and EVAP connections
Use a low-pressure smoke test to find a small leak
dontReplaceYet: EVAP canister before confirming leak location
Fuel tank or valves without testing

title: Coolant thermostat temperature below regulating temperature
meaning: The engine is taking longer than expected to reach its normal operating temperature. A thermostat that stays open is one possible cause.
safeToDriveNote: A short drive is typically possible if the temperature gauge stays normal, but have it checked; stop if the engine overheats or coolant is low.

causes.name: Coolant temperature sensor or wiring issue
Low coolant or cooling-system issue
causes.notes: Check level only when safe and cool.

mechanicChecklist: Check coolant level when the engine is cool
Compare coolant temperature readings during warm-up
Test thermostat operation and sensor circuit
dontReplaceYet: Coolant temperature sensor before confirming its readings
Water pump unless there are supporting symptoms or test results

title: Intake air temperature sensor circuit high input
meaning: The computer is seeing an unusually high voltage from the intake-air temperature sensor circuit, often interpreted as very cold air. This may affect fueling.
safeToDriveNote: It is typically possible to drive gently if the engine runs normally, but have the sensor circuit checked soon; stop if it stalls or runs very roughly.

causes.name: Sensor connector unplugged or poor connection
Open circuit or damaged wiring
causes.notes: Check circuit continuity and reference voltage.

causes.name: Failed intake-air temperature sensor
causes.notes: Compare scan reading to ambient temperature.

mechanicChecklist: Compare intake-air temperature reading with ambient temperature
Inspect connector and wiring
Test sensor resistance and circuit before replacing
dontReplaceYet: MAF sensor unless its own tests indicate a fault
Engine computer before checking wiring and sensor

title: Crankshaft position sensor circuit malfunction
meaning: The computer is not receiving the expected signal from the crankshaft position circuit. Starting or engine operation may be affected.
safeToDriveNote: The engine may stall or fail to restart; avoid a trip if starting or running is unreliable and arrange prompt diagnosis.

causes.name: Damaged wiring or poor electrical connection
causes.notes: Check harness near heat or moving parts.

causes.name: Trigger wheel or mechanical timing issue
causes.notes: Check if wiring and sensor signal are sound.

mechanicChecklist: Check stored and pending codes and freeze-frame data
Inspect sensor connector and harness
Scope or test crankshaft signal during cranking
dontReplaceYet: Crankshaft sensor before confirming power, ground, and signal
Engine computer before checking wiring and trigger signal

title: Camshaft position sensor circuit malfunction
meaning: The computer is not receiving the expected signal from a camshaft position circuit. Starting, timing, or engine performance can be affected.
safeToDriveNote: If it starts and runs normally, a short trip is typically possible, but have it checked soon; avoid driving if it stalls or loses power.

causes.name: Timing or reluctor target issue
causes.notes: Check if sensor and wiring tests pass.

mechanicChecklist: Check related crankshaft or timing codes
Inspect sensor connector, wiring, and ground
Verify camshaft signal and mechanical timing as needed
dontReplaceYet: Camshaft sensor before confirming circuit and signal
Timing components without supporting diagnostic results

title: Mass or volume air flow sensor range/performance
meaning: The measured airflow does not match what the computer expects. An intake leak or airflow sensor issue may affect engine performance.
safeToDriveNote: It is typically possible to drive gently if the engine runs normally, but have it checked soon; stop if it stalls or loses significant power.

causes.name: Air leak after the airflow sensor
Dirty or inaccurate MAF sensor
causes.notes: Check readings and contamination using approved methods.

causes.name: Blocked air filter or wiring fault

mechanicChecklist: Inspect intake ducting for leaks or damage
Check air filter and MAF wiring
Compare live airflow data with engine load
dontReplaceYet: MAF sensor before checking for leaks and wiring
Oxygen sensors without fuel-trim evidence

title: Mass or volume air flow sensor circuit low input
meaning: The airflow sensor circuit is reporting a signal lower than expected. This can affect the engine's fuel calculation.
safeToDriveNote: A short drive is typically possible if the engine runs smoothly, but arrange a check soon; stop if it stalls or loses power.
mechanicChecklist: Check MAF connector, power, ground, and wiring
Inspect air filter and intake ducting
Test airflow signal before sensor replacement
dontReplaceYet: MAF sensor without electrical and live-data checks
Engine computer before checking circuit wiring

title: Exhaust gas recirculation flow insufficient
meaning: The exhaust-gas recirculation system is not flowing as much as the computer expects. This may affect emissions or cause hesitation.
safeToDriveNote: It is typically drivable if the engine runs normally, but have it checked; stop if it stalls, overheats, or loses substantial power.

causes.name: EGR valve not opening fully
causes.notes: Test commanded operation and position feedback.

causes.name: Control hose, wiring, or sensor issue
causes.notes: Check the system design for the vehicle.

mechanicChecklist: Check related codes and EGR command data
Test EGR valve operation and feedback
Inspect passages for restriction and check control circuit
dontReplaceYet: EGR valve before checking passages and control circuit
Intake manifold without evidence of a restriction

title: Idle air control system malfunction
meaning: The engine computer cannot control idle speed as expected. The engine may idle too high, too low, or unevenly.
safeToDriveNote: If the engine stays running and responds normally, a short trip is typically possible; avoid driving if it stalls in traffic or idle is unpredictable.

causes.name: Dirty or sticking idle control passage or valve
causes.notes: Inspect according to the vehicle procedure.

mechanicChecklist: Record idle speed and symptoms cold and warm
Check intake for vacuum leaks
Test idle control circuit and inspect throttle/air passages
dontReplaceYet: Idle control valve before checking leaks and wiring
Throttle body before confirming the fault source

title: Transmission control system request
meaning: The engine computer has been told that the transmission controller has stored a fault. This code is a notice; transmission-specific codes are needed to identify the issue.
safeToDriveNote: Driving behavior depends on the underlying transmission fault. If shifting is harsh, slipping, or a warning is present, avoid driving and arrange diagnosis promptly.

causes.name: Transmission controller has a separate stored code
causes.notes: Read codes from the transmission module with a capable scanner.

mechanicChecklist: Scan the transmission control module for its own codes
Record shift symptoms and warning messages
Check fluid condition and level using the vehicle procedure
dontReplaceYet: Transmission or controller before retrieving transmission-specific codes
Solenoids before confirming the related fault and test results

title: Oxygen sensor slow response (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
meaning: The upstream oxygen sensor is responding more slowly than expected. The sensor may be aging, but mixture problems or wiring can also affect the signal.
safeToDriveNote: It is typically drivable if the engine runs normally, but arrange diagnosis; stop if the warning flashes, the engine runs roughly, or power drops.

causes.name: Mixture problem affecting sensor response
causes.notes: Check fuel trims and related codes.

mechanicChecklist: Check for exhaust leaks and related mixture codes
Review oxygen sensor response data
Inspect wiring and connector before sensor replacement
dontReplaceYet: Catalytic converter based on this code alone
Oxygen sensor without confirming slow response

title: Oxygen sensor heater circuit malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
meaning: The heater circuit for the upstream oxygen sensor has a fault. The heater helps the sensor reach operating temperature sooner.
safeToDriveNote: It is typically possible to drive if the vehicle runs normally, but have the circuit checked to avoid prolonged emissions issues.
mechanicChecklist: Check heater fuse and power supply
Inspect wiring and connector
Test heater element and control circuit
dontReplaceYet: Oxygen sensor before checking fuse, power, and wiring
Engine computer before circuit tests

title: Oxygen sensor heater circuit malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
meaning: The heater circuit for the downstream oxygen sensor has a fault. This sensor is generally used to monitor emissions-system performance.
safeToDriveNote: It is typically drivable if the engine runs normally, but have the electrical fault checked and address any other codes first.

causes.name: Wiring, connector, or fuse issue
causes.notes: Inspect for heat or road damage.

mechanicChecklist: Check for exhaust and heater-related codes
Inspect wiring near the exhaust
Test fuse, power, ground, and heater resistance
dontReplaceYet: Catalytic converter before addressing sensor heater fault
Sensor before checking wiring and fuse

title: Evaporative emission control system malfunction
meaning: The fuel-vapor system did not complete its leak check as expected. More specific tests are needed to find whether a valve, leak, or circuit is involved.
safeToDriveNote: It is typically drivable if there is no fuel odor and the engine runs normally; have it checked if the light remains on.
mechanicChecklist: Inspect fuel cap and filler neck
Check EVAP hoses, valves, and wiring
Run system leak and function tests
dontReplaceYet: EVAP canister before locating the fault
Purge valve without a functional test

title: Evaporative emission vent control circuit malfunction
meaning: The vent control circuit for the fuel-vapor system is not operating as expected. A valve, wiring, or blocked vent may be involved.
safeToDriveNote: It is typically drivable if there is no fuel odor and normal engine operation; arrange a check, especially if refueling is difficult.

causes.name: Vent valve or filter restricted
causes.notes: Check for dirt, water, or blockage.

causes.name: Vent valve wiring or connector fault

mechanicChecklist: Inspect vent valve, filter, and hoses
Check wiring and connector at the valve
Test valve command and circuit response
dontReplaceYet: EVAP canister before checking vent path
Vent valve without circuit and blockage tests

title: Oxygen sensor circuit low voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
meaning: The upstream oxygen-sensor signal is lower than expected. This can reflect a lean mixture, a sensor issue, or wiring trouble.
safeToDriveNote: If the engine runs normally, a short trip is typically possible, but arrange diagnosis; stop if it stalls or runs very roughly.

causes.name: Lean mixture or intake leak
causes.notes: Review fuel trims and check for air leaks.

causes.name: Oxygen sensor fault
causes.notes: Confirm response after mixture and wiring checks.

mechanicChecklist: Check fuel trims and intake for leaks
Inspect sensor wiring and exhaust leaks
Test sensor signal under operating conditions
dontReplaceYet: Oxygen sensor before checking for lean conditions and wiring
Catalytic converter based on this code alone

title: Engine coolant temperature sensor circuit high input
meaning: The coolant-temperature circuit is reporting a higher voltage than expected, often interpreted as an unusually cold reading. Verify the sensor and circuit.
safeToDriveNote: If the temperature gauge behaves normally and the engine runs well, a short trip is typically possible; monitor temperature and stop if it overheats.

causes.name: Coolant temperature sensor fault
causes.notes: Compare scan reading to actual temperature.

mechanicChecklist: Compare scan temperature with ambient before start
Inspect coolant level when safe and inspect connector
Test sensor resistance and wiring continuity
dontReplaceYet: Thermostat before verifying temperature sensor data
Engine computer before circuit checks

title: Throttle position sensor circuit low input
meaning: The throttle-position circuit is reporting a lower signal than expected. The vehicle may have reduced power or an inconsistent response.
safeToDriveNote: If throttle response is unpredictable or power is limited, avoid driving and arrange prompt diagnosis; otherwise have it checked soon.

causes.name: Wiring short or poor reference voltage

mechanicChecklist: Check for reduced-power warnings and related codes
Inspect throttle connector and wiring
Compare throttle position data through pedal movement
dontReplaceYet: Throttle body before checking sensor signal and wiring
Engine computer before circuit tests

title: Vehicle speed sensor malfunction
meaning: The computer is not receiving a reliable vehicle-speed signal. The speedometer, shifting, or stability systems may be affected.
safeToDriveNote: If the speedometer or shifting is unreliable, avoid driving in traffic and have it checked promptly; vehicle behavior varies by model.

causes.name: Speed sensor or connector fault
causes.notes: Check signal at sensor and module.

causes.name: Related ABS or transmission signal fault

mechanicChecklist: Check speedometer and related warning lights
Scan ABS and transmission modules for related codes
Inspect sensor wiring and verify speed signal
dontReplaceYet: Transmission before checking speed sensor signal and wiring
Speed sensor without verifying the source and circuit
